sport.title: How Aryna Sabalenka’s record and prize money from the 2026 WTA season compares to 2025
paras: After losing the Australian Open final to Elena Rybakina , the former world number one bounced back emphatically, winning Indian Wells and the Miami Open. At the time, it seemed the Belarusian would go on to dominate proceedings on the WTA Tour throughout 2026.

Sabalenka went on to suffer a plethora of early exits at significant WTA Tour events: including a concerning defeat to Diana Shnaider at the French Open , and a worrisome performance against Jessica Pegula in Berlin. Sabalenka has done little to improve her situation since the summer , and has now fallen to world number three for the first time since August 12, 2024.

sport.title: Jessica Pegula suggests the main reason why she lost to Mirra Andreeva at the WTA Finals
paras: Jessica Pegula has exited the WTA Finals after a semifinal defeat to Mirra Andreeva. Andreeva surprised herself against Pegula , who she beat 6-3, 6-4 after one hour and 25 minutes. Despite the superb victory, Andreeva still doesn’t understand how Pegula plays .

But that matters not right now as the Russian teenager turns her focus to her experienced WTA rival Elina Svitolina. They will meet in the final of the WTA Finals , having already played against each other in the group stage. Meanwhile, Pegula has been left wondering what could have been at Indian Wells, where the crowd were eager to see a home favourite emerge.

sport.title: Mirra Andreeva has message for Elina Svitolina in winner’s speech immediately after beating her at the WTA Fin
paras: Mirra Andreeva has sent a heartfelt message of commiserations to Elina Svitolina after beating her in the final of the WTA Finals. After one hour and 48 minutes in Indian Wells, Andreeva defeated Svitolina 7-5, 6-3 to secure the title.

The Russian superstar has emerged victorious on her WTA Finals debut. But rather than focus on her own stunning success, Andreeva was quick to praise Svitolina after their exciting encounter. In a classy winner’s speech, the 19-year-old said to her opponent: “I just want to congratulate Elina and the team for an amazing week.

sport.title: Mirra Andreeva Sinks Svitolina To Become Youngest WTA Finals Champion Since Sharapova
paras: Mirra Andreeva capped off her dream run at the WTA Finals with a tightly contested two-set triumph over Elina Svitolina to win the title on her tournament debut. The 19-year-old battled to a 7-5, 6-3 win over 2018 champion Svitolina during what was a roller-coaster encounter in Indian Wells.

A total of nine breaks occurred during the 109-minute match, with six of those being in Andreeva’s favour. Overall, she converted six out of 16 break point opportunities. “Coming into this match, it was the second time in my life where I thought that I’m just gonna die on the court, she’s not getting the win,” Andreeva told Sky Sports.

sport.title: Mirra Andreeva issues strong message after winning the WTA Finals, ‘she is not getting the win’
paras: The Russian youngster maintained her flawless status at the end-of-year event, beating Elina Svitolina 7-5, 6-3 in Sunday’s final. It was another superb performance by the young Russian, who has also defeated Aryna Sabalenka, Diana Shnaider and Jessica Pegula in the past week.

Andreeva was particularly effective off the return, winning 52 per cent of all points off Svitolina’s first serve, as reported by Sofascore . “It was the second time in my life where I just thought I am going to die on the court but she is not getting the win,” Andreeva told Sky Sports in the immediate aftermath of Sunday’s blockbuster.

sport.title: 19-year-old Andreeva storms to WTA Finals title on debut without dropping a set
paras: In Indian Wells, the 19-year-old Russian completed a perfect week by beating the 2018 champion for the second time in six days. She is the first teenager to win the WTA Finals since Maria Sharapova in 2004.

Mirra Andreeva has capped an outstanding 2026 season, marked by a first Grand Slam title, by winning the WTA Finals. The 19-year-old Russian beat Elina Svitolina 7-5, 6-3 in the final on Sunday night in Indian Wells, closing out the match at her second match point when the Ukrainian missed a smash. Andreeva completes a perfect first appearance at the WTA Finals : five matches, five wins, not a set dropped, even if the final was less one-sided than the rest of her run.
